data.narrative:
Overview Energy, a Seed-stage space and aerospace company founded by Marc Berte and Andrew Cantino, has raised $20M to date. The broader Space & Aerospace sector comprises 5 public comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers including SpaceX, Rocket Lab, and ICEYE, though the immediate peer set at identical stage and valuation tier remains limited.

Valuation analysis relies on stage-progression methodology, applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-Series A transitions to the $20M total raised proxy, yielding $50M as the base implied valuation. Public-comp anchoring cannot be applied absent disclosed revenue figures, which are standard for private companies. Peer-median triangulation is not viable given insufficient narrow-filter matches (fewer than 3 same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables with similar valuation tier), making sector-wide medians unreliable as calibration points.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $42M to $57M, with $50M as the midpoint. This reflects execution risk inherent to early-stage frontier technology and reliance on a single applicable method. Key uncertainties include capital intensity and runway relative to typical Seed progression in aerospace, revenue trajectory, and technical milestone achievement. Investor conviction should be weighted heavily on foundational technology viability and management track record rather than comparable value signals, which remain sparse at this stage.
